name: Deep Lilac
lede: Deep Lilac is a saturated violet-purple, the 2010 xkcd survey's darker, richer version of plain [[lilac]].

sections.title: Lilac, intensified
sections.body:
Our only recorded source for this name is the 2010 xkcd crowd color survey; no book or earlier dictionary in our data carries it [1]. Converted to the ISCC-NBS 1955 system, it falls nearest to the block the dictionary calls "brilliant violet", though 7.5 units away, a looser match than most names in our library [2]. In Munsell terms it reads about 3.2P 5.2/11.0, a mid-dark, strongly saturated purple [2].

The lilac flower itself is pale and slightly pink-grey; "deep" here, as with its sibling [[deep-lavender]], moves the word away from the real flower toward a bolder purple [2]. The two names sit only a few color units apart, close enough to be mistaken for each other on screen [2]. Where exactly this modifier pairing was first used is undocumented in the sources we hold [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: As with Deep Lavender, this exact shade does not turn up in any of the 23,781 paintings in our archive within our matching threshold, as photographed [3]. Vivid, fully saturated violets like this are uncommon in historical paint, which leaned on greyer, earthier purple pigments [3]. The absence is a computed color comparison against museum photographs, not proof that no painter ever mixed anything like it [3].
